content: To achieve the maximum benefit from this medication, it is important to use it regularly as prescribed. Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before using golimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Golimumab may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using golimumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, you should undergo regular lab and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, and skin exams. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it later for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Store the medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. If necessary, the medication may also be stored at room temperature. However, if stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator, and discard it after 30 days. Discard any unused portion after use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Your medical condition may cause complications in a medical emergency. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
